html:
The League of Nations was the first worldwide organisation of states set up to keep the peace. It was created by the peace conference after the First World War, began work in January 1920, and was based in Geneva in Switzerland.

Its members promised to settle quarrels by talks and to act together against an aggressor. The American president Woodrow Wilson had pushed for it, but the US Senate refused to join, which weakened it from the start.

The League also handed out the colonies of the defeated powers as "mandates", to be ruled by the winners until they were judged ready to govern themselves:

  • Former Ottoman lands: Syria and Lebanon went to France, Iraq and Palestine to Britain.
  • Former German colonies: Togoland and Kamerun were split between Britain and France, Ruanda-Urundi went to Belgium and South West Africa to South Africa.

The League settled some small disputes and did useful work on health, refugees and labour. But it failed against the big powers. It did little when Japan seized Manchuria in 1931, and when Italy invaded Ethiopia in 1935 its sanctions were weak; Haile Selassie's appeal to it in 1936 became famous. It could not stop the Second World War, and in 1946 it handed its work to the new United Nations.
sum: The League of Nations was the first worldwide organisation of states set up to keep the peace. It was created by the peace conference after the First World War, began work in January 1920, and was based in Geneva in Switzerland.
